subject: platform/devlog
professional: a senior build/tooling engineer who owns a static-site generator and its internal reporting pages (checks first: do the numbers on the page equal the source files, is the Markdown renderer safe and standards-faithful, would a regression be caught)

evidence.correctness: Ran collect() on the real repo and recomputed four outputs with independent code (grep and a separate Python script, not the module): experiments 121 (grep -c '^## E[0-9]*:' = 121); run records 5649 (ls prompts/runs/*.json = 5649) with outcomes success 5049 / partial 596 / failed 4 and top friction file research/CLAUDE.md = 474, CLAUDE.md = 344, 396 distinct files (Python Counter matched exactly); backlog 63 files, status done 49 / open 10 / dropped 4 (matched); studies 33 READMEs = 33 (matched). Reports+drift 34 docs = 36 .md files minus 2 READMEs (matched). Counting is right. Wrong outputs found in edge logic: verdictOf('not helped') returns 'helped', verdictOf('helped in 2 of 5; worse in 3') returns 'helped', and a Result starting with '(' is always 'pending' even when it carries a real result ('(verification only; ...' in prompts/experiments.md). On the real data this changes at most a few of 121 rows, but the page's headline is built on it. Not 4: verdict classification is substring matching on free text.
evidence.completeness: README claims checked by running: build.mjs writes index.html, analyses.json, experiments/index.html and one page per report, drift report and study (node test 'the real repository renders every page' passes; publish-branch.sh line 329 calls build.mjs, as the README says). All six README sections (friction by file/day, experiments, backlog, reports, studies, integrity/deviations) are rendered from the named sources. Empty sources render empty, tested. No stubs or TODOs in the 5 source files. Minor: README says 'Markdown is escaped before formatting' but inline() applies link and code regexes to raw text and escapes after (see craft).
evidence.verification: node --test platform/devlog/*.test.mjs: 11 pass, 0 fail, 0.6 s. Mutation 1: reversed the examples date sort in summariseRuns (b.date -> a.date): 1 test failed (caught). Mutation 2: inverted the 'measured result' filter in headlines() in render.mjs: 11 pass, 0 fail (SURVIVED); headlines() is only tested on an empty repo (assert.deepEqual(headlines(a), [])), so the owner-facing headline sentences have no assertion on non-empty data. Mutation 3: changed title-drop heading level in renderMarkdown: caught. All reverted with git checkout; git status clean. Also untested: renderIndex numbers on non-empty data (the real-repo test only checks anchors exist), dayTable, verdicts beyond three phrases, tables with escaped pipes. 2 of 3 mutations caught, but the surviving one is in the owner-facing summary.
evidence.craft: Read devlog.mjs, markdown.mjs, render.mjs, build.mjs and the test file. Good: zero dependencies, pure functions with injectable now, malformed JSON skipped, HTML escaped in render.mjs everywhere via esc(), no script or off-origin loads. Defects: (1) inline() link regex [label](href) takes [^)\s]+ so a URL containing parentheses or a title ("[y](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foo_(bar))") renders as a broken link <a href=".../Foo_(bar"> followed by stray ')' and '[x](url "t")' leaks "t") text. (2) Table cells split on '|' so an escaped pipe \| splits the cell (renders x \ | y as two cells, shifting columns). (3) PR autolink #\d{3,5} also links issue numbers and codes like #12345 to /pull/. (4) textOf falls back to JSON.stringify of a non-standard entry, silent. (5) readStudies dates a study by its newest date string anywhere in the text, so a future-dated mention reorders it. (6) renderMarkdown module-level regexes are fine; no dead code found. Reviewer would accept with the Markdown limitations noted.
evidence.claims: Checked against files: 'a missing source renders an empty section, never a zero' backed by test and by existsSync guards (true). 'only http(s), in-page and repository links survive' backed by resolveHref and test (javascript: dropped; but a bare 'mailto:' is also dropped, fine). 'nothing is typed by hand' true for counts. 'Markdown is escaped before formatting (markdown.mjs)' is not accurate: code spans and links are cut from raw text first, escape comes after (the module header says 'Everything is escaped first' too); outcome is still safe because held HTML is built with esc(), but the claim is wrong as written. The page headline '121 of 121 logged experiments still read (next review)' is false: only 113 of 116 Result lines say '(next review)'; 5 experiments have no Result line at all and one result starts with '(verification only...)'. headlines() counts verdict==='pending', which conflates 'no Result' with 'next review'. The footer 'nothing here is typed by hand' is true. No disclaimer needed for an internal dev page. Two inaccurate statements, one of them a number the owner reads on the page.
evidence.fitness: Job: let the owner and later agents read what runs keep tripping on, experiment verdicts, backlog state and long reports on the Pages site. Walked it: built to a temp dir via the test, index lists tiles, headlines, friction by file with links to sources, per-document pages, analyses.json. It does that job with real numbers (5649 records, 396 friction files). Limit: the single most decision-relevant output, experiment verdicts, is 121/121 pending because no one fills Results; the tool surfaces that honestly but cannot tell 'unreviewed' from 'reviewed, no Result field'.
evidence.domain: Compared against CommonMark and standard static-report practice: it is a deliberate subset, not CommonMark. Departures: no link titles, no balanced parentheses in URLs (spec allows), no escaped pipes in GFM tables (GFM spec: \| is a literal pipe), emphasis via regex rather than delimiter runs, no reference links or HTML. Verdict extraction by keyword is not a defined data format: a structured 'Verdict:' field would be the practitioner choice. For an internal page that only renders the repo's own documents the subset is defensible, but a senior would use an audited library (marked/markdown-it with html disabled) or a tight, documented grammar plus a test corpus. Scored 2: works on its own documents, departs from the standard in ways the README does not list.

defects.what: headlines() reports '121 of 121 logged experiments still read (next review)' but only 113 of 116 Result lines read that, 5 experiments have no Result line, and verdict 'pending' conflates missing, '(next review)' and parenthesised real results
verdictOf matches substrings anywhere in free text: 'not helped' and 'helped in 2 of 5; worse in 3' classify as helped; a Result starting with '(' is always pending even if it holds a real result
headlines() has no test on non-empty data: inverting its 'measured result' filter leaves all 11 tests green
defects.where: platform/devlog/devlog.test.mjs (headlines only asserted on an empty repo), platform/devlog/render.mjs:103-106

defects.what: Markdown links with parentheses in the URL or a title render broken (<a href="...Foo_(bar"> plus stray text)
Escaped pipe in a table cell splits the cell, shifting columns
Module header and README say text is escaped before formatting; code escapes after cutting links and code spans (still safe because held HTML is built with esc())
#NNN autolink sends any 3 to 5 digit token to /pull/, including issue numbers and non-PR codes

verdict: A small, dependency-free, safely escaped report generator whose counting is correct: experiments (121), run records (5649), outcome split, friction ranking (research/CLAUDE.md 474), backlog status (49/10/4), studies (33) and doc counts all matched independent recomputation, and the 11 tests pass. It falls short of the bar on claims and verification: the page headline '121 of 121 ... still read (next review)' is not what the source says (113 of 116 Result lines; 5 experiments have none), verdict classification is keyword matching that reads 'not helped' as helped, and the headline sentences have no test on real-shaped data (one of three seeded mutations survived). The Markdown renderer is a documented-by-behaviour subset of CommonMark that mishandles parenthesised URLs and escaped pipes. Meets the finished mark (completeness 3) but not the bar: claims 2 and verification 2 are below 3. Cheap fixes: give headlines() a populated-fixture test, split pending into 'no result' and 'awaiting review', and word-boundary or first-clause the verdict match.
